boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten documented PLU spaces for making, studying, gathering, recreation, and campus events.

cards.title: Reserve a Mortvedt Library study room
cards.subtitle: Mortvedt Library, all floors
cards.notes: Book a room online for a private or group work session, then pick up its key at the circulation desk with your valid PLU ID.
cards.short_summary: Reservable rooms support private and group study throughout Mortvedt Library.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU states that study rooms on every library floor may be reserved for private and group study; a valid PLU email is required for online reservations.
cards.access_notes: Reservation requires a valid PLU email; key checkout requires a current valid PLU ID card.

cards.title: Settle into third-floor silent study
cards.subtitle: Mortvedt Library, Floor 3
cards.notes: Choose the third floor when you need a quiet reading or focused writing stretch; keep conversations elsewhere and use nearby study rooms as needed.
cards.short_summary: The library designates its third floor for silent study.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU's library policies designate the third floor of Mortvedt Library as Silent Study.
cards.access_notes: Follow library noise norms and check current library hours before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Mortvedt Library First-Floor Collaborative Study Area
cards.title: Work together on the library’s first floor
cards.subtitle: Mortvedt Library, Floor 1
cards.notes: Bring a project partner or study group to the first-floor collaborative area, where the library permits conversation while people work.
cards.short_summary: The first floor is Mortvedt Library’s designated collaborative study area.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU's library policies identify the first floor as a collaborative study area; the floor also houses the Digital Media Center and Center for Student Success.
cards.access_notes: Check current library hours before visiting; keep noise considerate of adjacent library users.

cards.title: Make a media project in Studio 017
cards.subtitle: Mortvedt Library, Room 017
cards.notes: Reserve Studio 017 for a small recording or photo session, and plan time to learn the setup before your group arrives.
cards.short_summary: A reservable library studio provides recording, lighting, and photography tools.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU describes The Library Studio in Mortvedt Library Room 017 as a reservable student space with recording equipment, lighting kits, backdrops, and room for six people to record.
cards.access_notes: Available to students, faculty, and staff during building hours; reserve through LibCal or the circulation desk.

cards.title: See what is showing at the Scandinavian Cultural Center
cards.subtitle: Anderson University Center, ground floor
cards.notes: Check the cultural center’s program before you go, then use its exhibitions or workshops as a starting point for a shared campus outing.
cards.short_summary: The ground-floor center combines exhibition galleries, a main hall, and cultural programs.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU identifies the Scandinavian Cultural Center as a ground-floor Anderson University Center museum and gathering space with exhibition galleries, programs, lectures, and workshops.
cards.source_title: Scandinavian Cultural Center at PLU: Preserving Heritage and Building Connections Across Communities | PLU News
cards.access_notes: Program and gallery access can vary by event; consult the center’s current information before visiting.

cards.title: Meet up on Centennial Plaza
cards.subtitle: Upper campus, outside the Karen Hille Phillips Center
cards.notes: Use the red-brick plaza as a clear meeting point before a campus program, then pause to notice the Centennial Bell across from the performing-arts center.
cards.short_summary: PLU’s central red-brick quadrangle is commonly called Red Square.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU says the red-brick quadrangle at the heart of campus is colloquially called Red Square and officially named Centennial Plaza.
cards.source_title: Elements of the Ceremony | Commencement | PLU
cards.access_notes: Outdoor plaza; event setups and weather may affect available space.

cards.title: Find the Centennial Bell
cards.subtitle: Centennial Plaza, across from the Karen Hille Phillips Center
cards.notes: Stop by the bell while crossing Red Square and connect the object with PLU’s opening-of-year Convocation and Commencement ceremonies.
cards.short_summary: The campus bell marks both the arrival of a new class and graduation ceremonies.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU documents that the Centennial Bell is on campus across from the Karen Hille Phillips Center and is rung for the first day of classes and ceremonially at Commencement.
cards.source_title: Elements of the Ceremony | Commencement | PLU
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus landmark; view respectfully and do not assume public bell-ringing access.

cards.title: Plan a game on Foss Field
cards.subtitle: PLU campus recreation field
cards.notes: Look for an intramural schedule or gather a group for permitted field activity; the recreation program lists several sports for this outdoor space.
cards.short_summary: Foss Field is a PLU recreation site for several intramural sports.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU Recreation lists Foss Field as a site for intramural soccer, flag football, softball, and ultimate frisbee.
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to recreation programming, field conditions, and any applicable campus scheduling rules.

cards.title: Walk the PLU Meadows Frisbee Golf Course
cards.subtitle: Behind Columbia Center and along the cross-country course
cards.notes: Start at the first hole behind Columbia Center and follow the course through the cross-country area; a practice hole sits behind Foss Hall.
cards.short_summary: The campus course begins behind Columbia Center and continues through the cross-country course.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU Recreation states that the first hole of the PLU Meadows Frisbee Golf Course is behind Columbia Center, with the course continuing through the cross-country course.
cards.access_notes: Bring appropriate equipment and yield to scheduled recreation or cross-country activity.

cards.title: Check Memorial Gym’s recreation options
cards.subtitle: Memorial Gymnasium / Names Fitness Center
cards.notes: Use the recreation schedule to find a basketball, dodgeball, or group-exercise opportunity in Memorial Gym before heading over.
cards.short_summary: Memorial Gym hosts intramural play and group exercise through PLU Recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU Recreation lists Memorial Gym as a location for dodgeball, basketball, group exercise classes, and the Names Fitness Center.
cards.access_notes: Building access and activity availability are subject to current recreation schedules and PLU access rules.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten currently documented, under-21-safe activities with free admission or participation for PLU students and the Tacoma community.

cards.title: Take a Foundations Yoga class
cards.subtitle: Anderson University Center, PLU
cards.notes: PLU students, faculty, and staff can join the free class; check the calendar listing for the scheduled AUC room before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A short, no-cost campus yoga session for the PLU community.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU lists Foundations Yoga as free and open to PLU students, faculty, and staff.
cards.source_title: Foundations Yoga – free class for PLU students, faculty, and staff
cards.access_notes: For PLU students, faculty, and staff; the listing provides dates and directs visitors to check the schedule for the AUC room.

cards.title: See the University Gallery
cards.subtitle: Ingram Hall, Pacific Lutheran University
cards.notes: Visit during the gallery’s listed weekday hours to view the rotating art program; confirm the current exhibition or arrange an appointment if needed.
cards.short_summary: A free campus gallery visit in Ingram Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU states that the University Gallery is free to visit and open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., or by appointment.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–4 p.m., or by appointment; check the gallery schedule for exhibitions.

cards.title: Walk through the Seymour Conservatory
cards.subtitle: Wright Park, Tacoma
cards.notes: Step inside the historic conservatory for a plant-focused visit, then continue through Wright Park’s arboretum on the same outing.
cards.short_summary: Free conservatory admission inside Wright Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Parks Tacoma lists admission to the W. W. Seymour Botanical Conservatory as free, with a suggested donation.
cards.access_notes: Admission is free; the agency notes a suggested $3 donation, which is optional.

cards.title: Walk the Tacoma Nature Center trails
cards.subtitle: Tacoma Nature Center preserve
cards.notes: Use the designated trail network for a wetlands-and-forest walk; follow posted preserve rules and plan to finish before the daily closing time.
cards.short_summary: A free self-guided nature walk through a 70-acre preserve.
cards.evidence_claim: Parks Tacoma states that general admission to the Tacoma Nature Center preserve is free and describes more than two miles of walking trails.
cards.access_notes: Trails are open daily from 8 a.m. to 30 minutes after sunset; stay on designated trails and do not bring pets.

cards.entity_name: Frank Herbert Trail at Dune Peninsula
cards.title: Loop the Frank Herbert Trail
cards.subtitle: Dune Peninsula at Point Defiance Park
cards.notes: Follow the paved loop around Dune Peninsula and look for embedded medallions along the trail; go during daylight hours and use the public path.
cards.short_summary: A daylight waterfront walk on Dune Peninsula.
cards.evidence_claim: Parks Tacoma invites visitors to wander Dune Peninsula daily during daylight hours and identifies the paved Frank Herbert Trail loop there.
cards.access_notes: Dune Peninsula is open daily during daylight hours; Parks Tacoma notes free parking.

cards.title: Join the Titlow Bird Walk
cards.subtitle: Titlow Park & Lodge, September 20, 2026
cards.notes: Meet the Park Guide at Titlow for the scheduled shore-and-forest bird walk; bring layers and arrive ready to walk at the listed start time.
cards.short_summary: A free guided bird walk at Titlow Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Parks Tacoma lists the September 20, 2026 Titlow Bird Walk as a free, all-ages guided walk.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled for September 20, 2026, 9–11 a.m.; listed as all ages and free.

cards.title: Learn about shrikes at Swan Creek
cards.subtitle: Swan Creek Park, October 4, 2026
cards.notes: Join the scheduled bird program and guided walk at Swan Creek; review park notices before leaving because parts of its trail system may close.
cards.short_summary: A free guided bird program and walk at Swan Creek Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Parks Tacoma lists Coffee with the Birds: Shrikes at Swan Creek Park on October 4, 2026 as free.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled for October 4, 2026, 9–11 a.m.; check Swan Creek’s current closure notices before visiting.

cards.title: Play tabletop games at Franklin Park
cards.subtitle: Senator Rosa Franklin Park, August 19 or 22, 2026
cards.notes: Drop in for the Park Guides’ tabletop games and coloring activities; choose either listed session and confirm timing before traveling to the park.
cards.short_summary: Free park-guided games and activities at Franklin Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Parks Tacoma lists Park Spotlight: Franklin Park as free and describes tabletop games, coloring sheets, and Park Guide activities.
cards.access_notes: Listed sessions are August 19, 4–6 p.m., and August 22, 3–5 p.m.; confirm the date you plan to attend.

cards.title: Watch the Summer Bash movie outdoors
cards.subtitle: STAR Center, August 21, 2026
cards.notes: Bring a blanket or lawn chair for the outdoor movie and arrive for the pre-movie activities; food trucks are present, but buying food is optional.
cards.short_summary: A free, family-friendly outdoor movie night.
cards.evidence_claim: Parks Tacoma lists Summer Bash at STAR Center as free and says it includes a movie, games, face painting, and other activities.
cards.access_notes: Friday, August 21, 2026, at 6:30 p.m.; lawn seating, with the listed movie beginning at dusk.

cards.title: Take the Point Defiance Bird Walk
cards.subtitle: Five Mile Drive Entrance, Point Defiance Park
cards.notes: Meet at the Five Mile Drive entrance for the Park Guide-led bird walk; wear walking-appropriate layers and check the event listing for the next date.
cards.short_summary: A recurring, free guided walk through Point Defiance shore and forest.
cards.evidence_claim: Parks Tacoma lists the Point Defiance Bird Walk as a free, all-ages Park Guide-led walk and includes an August 23, 2026 date.
cards.source_title: Point Defiance Park – Five Mile Drive Entrance Events
cards.access_notes: The listing schedules the August 23, 2026 walk for 8:30–10:30 a.m.; verify future dates on the venue calendar.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented PLU spaces for silent, collaborative, reservable, and technology-supported study.

cards.title: Mortvedt Library Third-Floor Silent Study
cards.subtitle: Mortvedt Library, Floor 3
cards.notes: Bring reading or focused writing upstairs and keep conversation out of the silent-study area; reservable study rooms are also on this floor.
cards.short_summary: A designated silent-study floor in the library.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU identifies the library’s third floor as Silent Study and lists study rooms on that floor.
cards.access_notes: Use during Mortvedt Library open hours; consult current library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Mortvedt Library Second-Floor Study Area
cards.subtitle: Mortvedt Library, Floor 2
cards.notes: Choose this floor for coursework that allows light conversation, and use its study rooms when your group needs a more private setup.
cards.short_summary: Library study space where light conversation is permitted.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU’s library policy designates the second floor for light conversation while studying; the floor also has study rooms.
cards.access_notes: Use during Mortvedt Library open hours; consult current library hours before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Mortvedt Library First-Floor Collaborative Study Area
cards.title: Mortvedt Library First-Floor Collaborative Study Area
cards.subtitle: Mortvedt Library, Floor 1
cards.notes: Set up a project meeting or shared work session on the collaborative first floor, near library support services and study rooms.
cards.short_summary: A collaborative study zone on the library’s first floor.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU designates Mortvedt Library’s first floor as a collaborative study area and lists study rooms there.
cards.access_notes: Use during Mortvedt Library open hours; consult current library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Mortvedt Library Third-Floor Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Mortvedt Library, Floor 3
cards.notes: Reserve a third-floor room for focused private or group work; plan ahead because reservations require a valid PLU email and ID for the key.
cards.short_summary: Reservable rooms paired with the library’s silent floor.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU lists study rooms on Floor 3; library policy says study rooms may be reserved for private and group study.
cards.access_notes: A valid PLU email is required to reserve; a current PLU ID is required to check out a room key. Reservations are limited to four hours daily.

cards.title: Mortvedt Library Second-Floor Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Mortvedt Library, Floor 2
cards.notes: Book a second-floor room when you need a contained space for a partner session, then return the key promptly to the circulation desk.
cards.short_summary: Reservable study rooms on Mortvedt’s second floor.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU lists study rooms on Floor 2 and states that library study rooms can be reserved for private and group study.
cards.access_notes: Reserve online with a valid PLU email; rooms may be reserved up to one week ahead, with a four-hour daily limit.

cards.title: Mortvedt Library First-Floor Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Mortvedt Library, Floor 1
cards.notes: Reserve a first-floor study room when a quieter boundary will help your project group stay organized beside the library’s collaborative area.
cards.short_summary: Reservable rooms on the library’s collaborative floor.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU lists study rooms on Floor 1 and says the rooms can be reserved for private and group study.
cards.access_notes: A valid PLU email is required for reservation and a current PLU ID is required to check out the room key.

cards.title: The Library Studio
cards.subtitle: Mortvedt Library, Room 017
cards.notes: Reserve Studio 017 for a media project when recording, photography, or a small production session will move your assignment forward.
cards.short_summary: A reservable six-person media-production studio.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU says the Library Studio in Mortvedt Library Room 017 has recording equipment, lighting, photography backdrops, and room for six people.
cards.access_notes: Available to PLU students, faculty, and staff; reserve during building hours through the Circulation Desk or the library reservation system.

cards.title: Mortvedt Design Lab
cards.subtitle: Mortvedt Library, Room 140
cards.notes: Use the Mac workstations for design-heavy coursework, then save time by bringing files ready for Adobe Creative Suite or other installed software.
cards.short_summary: An 18-Mac lab for digital design work.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU identifies Mortvedt Design Lab in LIBR 140 as an 18-Mac Mini lab with Adobe Creative Suite and other software.
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours; PLU members have swipe access. Faculty arranging group use should contact the Circulation Desk or iTech.

cards.title: Wiegand Design Lab
cards.subtitle: Morken Center, Room 115
cards.notes: Head to Morken 115 when six Adobe-equipped Macs fit your project workflow, especially for focused digital production rather than a general reading session.
cards.short_summary: A six-computer Adobe design lab in Morken.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU says Wiegand Design Lab is in Morken 115 and has six Mac computers equipped with Adobe Creative Suite.
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours; PLU members have swipe access.

cards.title: Harstad Study Room
cards.subtitle: Harstad Hall, Floor 2
cards.notes: Use this large second-floor room when you want to spread out across smaller study areas; confirm residence-hall access before you go.
cards.short_summary: A large residence-hall study room divided into smaller areas.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU identifies the Harstad Study Room as a large second-floor Harstad Hall room divided into smaller student study spaces.
cards.access_notes: PLU states students have access to residence halls until 10:00 PM; check current residence-hall access procedures before visiting.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten documented destinations on the Garfield Street corridor immediately beside Pacific Lutheran University, each with one specific reason to stop.

cards.title: The Parkland Mural
cards.subtitle: Garfield Street corridor, beside PLU
cards.notes: Walk the Garfield Street corridor to view the mural and use PLU’s tour page to learn how local groups collaborated on its creation.
cards.short_summary: A documented community-made public artwork.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU documents collaboration by students, schools, youth organizations, Rotary, Kiwanis, and the Garfield Street Business Association on the mural.
cards.source_title: The Parkland Mural | A Parkland Tour | PLU
cards.access_notes: View from the public Garfield Street corridor; confirm any event-specific access separately.

cards.title: 208 Garfield
cards.subtitle: Garfield Street corridor, beside PLU
cards.notes: Use the Garfield Street stop for a PLU-owned food-service destination; check the venue directly before planning a meal or pickup.
cards.short_summary: PLU’s named Garfield Street food destination.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU identifies 208 Garfield as PLU-owned on its Garfield Street guide.
cards.access_notes: Food and beverage purchases are optional; verify current service details with the venue.

cards.title: Farrelli's Pizza — Parkland
cards.subtitle: Garfield Street corridor, 210 Garfield St S
cards.notes: Plan a food stop at the Parkland location, whose official page lists a kids’ arcade alongside its dining space and current hours.
cards.short_summary: A Garfield Street restaurant with a small arcade.
cards.evidence_claim: Farrelli’s lists its Parkland location at 210 Garfield St S and describes a small arcade for kids.
cards.access_notes: Food purchases are required to dine; use the restaurant’s official page for current hours.

cards.title: Marzano Italian Restaurant
cards.subtitle: Garfield Street corridor, 516 Garfield St S
cards.notes: Reserve or check walk-in availability before dinner; the restaurant’s official site identifies this Garfield Street address as adjacent to PLU.
cards.short_summary: A dinner-only restaurant adjacent to PLU.
cards.evidence_claim: Marzano lists its address as 516 Garfield St S, says it is adjacent to Pacific Lutheran University, and posts dinner-only hours.
cards.access_notes: Dinner purchase required; the official site says reservations are recommended.

cards.title: Notes' Coffee Company
cards.subtitle: Garfield Street corridor, at Garfield and C Street
cards.notes: Use this corner as a coffee-and-sandwich stop, and look for the community-programming context documented by PLU when the business opened.
cards.short_summary: A documented Garfield-and-C Street coffeehouse.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU reported that Notes’ Coffee Company opened on the corner of Garfield and C Street with coffee and sandwiches.
cards.source_title: Notes’ Coffee Company: A coffee house seeking community on Garfield | PLU
cards.access_notes: Purchases are required for menu items; confirm current operations directly before visiting.

cards.title: Rise and Shine Cabaret Cafe
cards.subtitle: Garfield Street corridor, at Garfield and C Street
cards.notes: Check the café’s current menu or programming before you go; PLU student media documented vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free menu options.
cards.short_summary: A Garfield-and-C Street café with documented dietary options.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU’s Mast Media reported that Rise and Shine Cabaret Cafe, at Garfield and C Street, offered vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free menu options.
cards.source_title: Local Business Thrives Years After Covid | The Mast
cards.access_notes: Menu purchases are required; confirm current menu and event details with the business.

cards.title: Amorata Essentia Metaphysical Gift Shop
cards.subtitle: Garfield Street corridor, at Garfield and C Street
cards.notes: Pair this shop with the neighboring café stop and browse its documented plants, crystals, and holistic-wellness merchandise at your own pace.
cards.short_summary: A documented specialty shop at the Garfield-and-C corner.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU’s Mast Media reported that Amorata Essentia Metaphysical Gift Shop at Garfield and C Street sold plants, crystals, and holistic-wellness products.
cards.source_title: Local Business Thrives Years After Covid | The Mast
cards.access_notes: Purchases are optional; confirm current inventory and opening details directly with the shop.

cards.title: Cutty Sark Intimates
cards.subtitle: Garfield Street corridor, beside Rise and Shine Cabaret Cafe
cards.notes: Use this Garfield Street storefront as a photography-and-apparel stop; PLU student media documented its September 2024 opening and local placement.
cards.short_summary: A documented 2024 Garfield Street storefront.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU’s Mast Media reported that Cutty Sark Intimates opened on Garfield Street in September 2024 near the Cabaret Cafe.
cards.source_title: Garfield’s Welcoming New Boudoir Studio | The Mast
cards.access_notes: Retail purchases are optional; verify current storefront hours directly before visiting.

cards.title: Emerald City Smoothie — Parkland
cards.subtitle: Garfield Street corridor, Parkland
cards.notes: Choose this Garfield Street food-and-drink stop when a smoothie fits your plan; PLU student media documented the Parkland location’s opening.
cards.short_summary: A documented Garfield Street smoothie-shop addition.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU’s Mast Media reported Emerald City Smoothie as a new addition on Garfield Street in Parkland.
cards.source_title: Garfield Street gets tasty new addition | The Mast
cards.access_notes: Purchases are required for menu items; confirm current location and hours directly before visiting.

cards.title: Northern Pacific Coffee Company
cards.subtitle: Garfield Street corridor, beside PLU
cards.notes: Make this a coffee break on the corridor leading into campus; PLU’s hospitality guide identifies it as a recently reopened Garfield Street business.
cards.short_summary: A named coffee stop on PLU’s Garfield Street guide.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU’s hospitality guide identifies Northern Pacific Coffee Company as a recently reopened business on Garfield Street.
cards.access_notes: Purchases are required for menu items; confirm current service details directly with the business.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented PLU rituals and recurring campus traditions, from the first-day bell to Scandinavian celebrations.

cards.title: Sankta Lucia Fest
cards.subtitle: Scandinavian Cultural Center, Pacific Lutheran University
cards.notes: Watch for the return of this Swedish music, song, dance, and children’s-performance celebration; the center says it resumes in 2026.
cards.short_summary: PLU’s long-running Swedish Lucia celebration opens its campus Christmas season.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU says Sankta Lucia Fest has been an annual campus tradition for seventy years and marks the beginning of its Christmas season.
cards.access_notes: PLU’s page says the 2025 fest was cancelled and it will resume in 2026; check the center’s event details before attending.

cards.title: Norwegian Heritage Festival
cards.subtitle: Scandinavian Cultural Center, Pacific Lutheran University
cards.notes: Plan for the annual March festival and its cultural demonstrations, then use the event listing to confirm the year’s program and access.
cards.short_summary: A festival begun after King Olav V’s 1975 PLU visit became an annual campus tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU states that a Norwegian Heritage Festival staged for King Olav V’s 1975 visit became an annual tradition, with food, entertainment, vendors, crafts, and demonstrations.
cards.access_notes: Held annually in March according to PLU; consult the current event information for attendance details.

cards.title: Norwegian Christmas Service
cards.subtitle: Scandinavian Cultural Center, Pacific Lutheran University
cards.notes: Attend the candlelit service for Norwegian-language songs and scripture readings; verify the annual date and venue with the center first.
cards.short_summary: A Norwegian-language candlelight service that PLU has hosted annually since 1975.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU describes Julegudstjeneste as an annual campus event since 1975, blending Norwegian spiritual songs and scripture readings.
cards.access_notes: Hosted by the Scandinavian Cultural Center; consult its current events information before attending.

cards.title: Nordic Christmas Fest
cards.subtitle: Scandinavian Cultural Center, Pacific Lutheran University
cards.notes: Look for the center’s annual Julefest invitation and current attendance details; it combines a holiday meal, conversation, and entertainment.
cards.short_summary: A Nordic holiday banquet that the Scandinavian Cultural Center has held for more than two decades.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU identifies Nordic Christmas Fest (Julefest) as an annual Scandinavian Cultural Center tradition that has run for over two decades.
cards.access_notes: PLU says members receive invitations; confirm eligibility, reservations, and cost with the Scandinavian Cultural Center.

cards.title: Syttende Mai Flag Raising
cards.subtitle: Red Square, Pacific Lutheran University
cards.notes: On May 17, join the morning Red Square gathering to raise the Norwegian and U.S. flags and sing the two national songs.
cards.short_summary: PLU marks Norwegian Constitution Day with a Red Square flag-raising tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU says students, faculty, and friends gather in Red Square on May 17 to raise Norwegian and U.S. flags and sing “Ja, vi elsker dette landet” and “The Star-Spangled Banner.”
cards.access_notes: PLU describes this as a morning celebration; confirm the current year’s start time and any following program.

cards.title: Summer Berry Festival
cards.subtitle: Red Square, Pacific Lutheran University
cards.notes: Check the summer dates, then stop by Red Square for the monthly fruit-themed gathering while free desserts remain available.
cards.short_summary: PLU’s oldest summer tradition cycles through strawberry, raspberry, and blueberry gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU calls the Berry Festival one of its oldest summer traditions; its Hospitality Services page describes monthly summer events featuring local-fruit desserts.
cards.access_notes: PLU lists the events in Red Square and says fresh fruit desserts are free while supplies last; dates are marked 2026 TBA.

cards.title: Bjug Day of Giving
cards.subtitle: Pacific Lutheran University
cards.notes: Follow the annual giving-day updates to learn the year’s projects and participate only if a donation fits your own budget and preferences.
cards.short_summary: An annual PLU giving day named for founder Rev. Bjug Harstad.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU describes Bjug Day of Giving as a big-hearted annual tradition named for its founder, Rev. Bjug Harstad, when Lutes support areas they value.
cards.access_notes: Participation is optional and may involve a donation; see PLU’s current Bjug Day information for timing and giving options.

cards.title: Opening Convocation
cards.subtitle: Olson Gym, Pacific Lutheran University
cards.notes: On the first fall-semester day, follow orientation guidance for the welcome procession and ceremony that formally opens the academic year.
cards.short_summary: PLU begins the academic year with a faculty welcome and a first-day convocation.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU describes Convocation as a unique tradition held on the first day of each fall semester, when professors line up to welcome new students and join the opening ceremony.
cards.source_title: First day of school tradition at PLU | Admission | PLU
cards.access_notes: The 2026 orientation schedule lists Convocation as a required opening-of-year tradition in Olson Gym; follow current orientation instructions.

cards.title: Ring in the New Class
cards.subtitle: Centennial Plaza (Red Square), Pacific Lutheran University
cards.notes: Gather in Red Square during LUTE Welcome for the bell ringing and procession to Convocation; use the current orientation schedule for timing.
cards.short_summary: The Centennial Bell announces a new class and the start of PLU’s academic year.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU states that the Centennial Bell is rung on the first day of classes to announce the new class and the beginning of Convocation.
cards.source_title: Elements of the Ceremony | Commencement | PLU
cards.access_notes: PLU’s Fall 2026 orientation schedule calls bell ringing and processing to Convocation an annual tradition in Red Square.

cards.title: The Mace Leads Commencement
cards.subtitle: PLU Commencement ceremony, Pacific Lutheran University
cards.notes: At commencement, notice the University Marshal carry PLU’s mace at the start of the academic procession and ceremonial display.
cards.short_summary: PLU’s commencement procession uses a custom mace to represent academic authority and independence.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU states that its University Marshal carries the PLU mace at the beginning of the Academic Procession, representing the university’s academic authority and independence.
cards.source_title: Elements of the Ceremony | Commencement | PLU
cards.access_notes: This tradition occurs as part of PLU’s commencement ceremony; consult the current commencement program for public attendance information.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Pacific Lutheran University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure first-weekend sequence that combines campus orientation, a meal, activity options, and ways to meet people.

cards.title: Start at the Anderson University Center
cards.subtitle: Campus hub for student life
cards.notes: Begin by walking through the AUC and noting Student Engagement locations. Use the building as a practical reference point before branching out across campus.
cards.short_summary: Use the student-life hub to get oriented.
cards.evidence_claim: PLU lists Student Engagement, Leadership, and Clubs/Organizations in Anderson University Center 161.
cards.source_title: Student Life and Campus Resources | PLU Catalog
